manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Compute sums, differences, products and quotients of signed integers and explain the sign of each result.
Evaluate expressions containing more than one integer operation in the correct sequence.
Model and solve practical problems involving gains, losses, temperature changes or positions below zero.
Explain when signed integers are useful for describing everyday quantities.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can signed integers represent changes and help us make calculations?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Use paired number cards, marked number lines and temperature records to model each operation; compare answers and explain combined steps.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Observe accurate integer operations, justified signs and an explanation of a real situation.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Determine cubes of suitable numbers through repeated multiplication and relate the calculation to cubic volume.
Find cube values accurately using mathematical tables.
Obtain cube roots of perfect cubes through factor-based reasoning.
Use mathematical tables to identify cube roots and check their relationship with cubes.
Calculate cubes and cube roots with a calculator and check that the operation is appropriate.
Use cubes or cube roots to resolve a practical measurement or volume question.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How are a number's cube and its cube root related, and when is each useful?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Build cubes from unit blocks; compare the number of blocks with repeated multiplication; use factors, tables and calculators to verify.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Check a written cubing method, factorised cube root, table reading and contextual volume result.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving
units.source_review_requirement: Compare all paraphrased targets with official PDF text and section/page references before any canonical promotion.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Represent repeated multiplication with a base and exponent, explaining what each symbol means.
Investigate patterns that establish rules for multiplying and dividing powers with a common base.
Simplify numerical expressions by applying the relevant index laws correctly.
Link powers of ten to common logarithms as inverse descriptions of the same relationship.
Give meaningful examples of where index notation or logarithms simplify a practical calculation.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: Why are powers useful for representing quantities, and how do logarithms relate to powers of ten?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Expand and regroup products of powers to justify index rules; build a base-ten power table; compare values using mathematical tables or devices.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess equivalent powers, correctly justified index-law steps and powers-of-ten/logarithm correspondence.

units.sub_strand: Compound Proportions and Rates of Work

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Divide a given amount into specified proportional shares and express each share clearly.
Compare proportional quantities by forming and interpreting ratios.
Solve compound-proportion questions using a clearly explained ratio method.
Calculate how amounts of work, numbers of workers and completion times relate under stated assumptions.
Explain why proportional reasoning and work-rate calculations support decisions in daily life.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How do changes in several quantities affect a proportional share or the time taken to finish a task?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Split counters or a sample budget in given ratios, then compare work scenarios with different team sizes; use ratio tables and digital practice.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Check each proportion and unit, explanations of direct or inverse relationships and reasonableness of work-rate answers.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Recognise an arrangement of entries in rows and columns as a matrix.
Describe a matrix by its number of rows and columns.
Locate and identify an element by its row and column position.
Determine whether two matrices have compatible orders for addition or subtraction.
Add or subtract matrices of the same order entry by entry with a meaningful context.
Explain how a matrix can organise real-world information.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How does a rectangular arrangement of information help us compare or combine data?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Organise results, shopping quantities or travel schedules into rectangular arrays; label row/column positions and combine equivalent tables.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess matrix order, item position, matching dimensions and each calculated entry.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Identify gradient as a measure of steepness in examples from the surroundings.
Calculate gradient from coordinates of two distinct points.
Form the equation of a straight line from two given points.
Form a straight-line equation using a point and a known gradient.
Rearrange a linear equation to identify its gradient and intercept in y = mx + c form.
Interpret the meaning of m, c and the variables in a straight-line model.
Find the horizontal and vertical axis intercepts of a straight line.
Explain a practical situation represented by a straight-line equation.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can a straight-line equation describe steepness and position on a graph?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Compare slopes of ramps or stairs; find differences in coordinates; derive equations from selected points and confirm intercepts on a graph.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess gradients, equations from both required forms, m/c interpretation and correct x-/y-intercepts.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving
units.source_review_requirement: Compare all paraphrased targets with official PDF text and section/page references before any canonical promotion.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Solve a linear inequality containing one unknown and interpret the valid values.
Represent a one-variable inequality on a number line or suitable graph.
Draw the boundary and solution region for a linear inequality in two variables.
Model a practical lower or upper limit with an inequality and check possible solutions.
Explain how inequalities help describe real-world constraints.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can a graph show every value that satisfies a restriction?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Translate a spending limit into algebra, test values, graph boundary lines and shade permissible regions using paper or digital graphing.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Look for correctly transformed inequalities, open/closed boundaries and correctly shaded feasible regions.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Determine the area of pentagonal and hexagonal plane figures by appropriate decomposition.
Find the surface areas of triangular and rectangular-based prisms.
Calculate surface area of pyramids with triangular, rectangular or square bases.
Determine areas of circular sectors and circular segments using the stated dimensions.
Work out curved and total surface areas of cones where relevant.
Calculate the surface area of a sphere using its radius or diameter.
Relate area calculations to real objects and explain the units used.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can flat shapes and nets help calculate areas of complex objects?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Cut regular polygons into simpler shapes, draw prism/pyramid/cone nets and measure circular sectors and balls.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess correct decomposition, units, and surface-area or sector formula selection.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Calculate the volume of prisms with triangular or rectangular bases.
Determine the volume of pyramids having triangular, rectangular or square bases.
Use dimensions to calculate the volume of a cone in an everyday setting.
Work out the volume of a frustum by comparing or subtracting appropriate solids.
Calculate the volume of spherical objects with correct cubic units.
Describe a situation where solid volume or capacity matters.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can the shape and dimensions of a solid determine its volume?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Measure model containers; compare prism and pyramid capacities; decompose a frustum and verify volumes using appropriate models.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess diagrams, substitution into correct solid-volume formulas and contextual interpretation.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Convert accurately among commonly used units of mass.
Differentiate mass from weight and describe how they are related.
Use measurements of mass and volume to determine a material's density.
Apply density calculations to a practical comparison of substances.
Explain why density is relevant in daily activities.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: Why may equal-sized objects have different masses, and how can density help explain this?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Use a weighing instrument and volume measurements to compare objects, convert units, and calculate density with a calculator as appropriate.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Check unit conversions, density = mass/volume reasoning, and distinction between mass and weight.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Find speed using distance and time and express it in kilometres per hour or metres per second.
Calculate average speed for a journey or timed activity.
Distinguish velocity from speed by including direction where appropriate.
Determine acceleration from a change in velocity over time.
Identify and locate lines of longitude on a globe or map.
Relate longitude differences to differences in local time.
Calculate the local time of places whose longitudes are supplied.
Explain how time and distance measurements support everyday tasks.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can movement be described mathematically, and why does local time change with longitude?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Time a safe walking or running distance; compute speed and acceleration; use a globe and maps to investigate longitude and local time.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Check speed, average-speed, velocity and acceleration distinctions, unit conversion and longitude/time arithmetic.
units.core_competency_focus: mathematical reasoning, collaboration and practical problem-solving

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Recognise and identify the currencies used by selected countries.
Convert between currencies using a supplied exchange rate.
Calculate export duty on goods from a stated customs scenario and rate.
Calculate import duty from given customs value and duty rate.
Determine excise duty for goods or services using supplied rules.
Calculate value-added tax for taxable goods or services using a specified rate.
Explain how currency exchange and taxes affect everyday purchases or trade.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: Why do people exchange currencies, and how are taxes on goods determined?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Study currency examples and dated exchange-rate information; interpret sample invoices, customs values and receipts to calculate duties and VAT.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess correct exchange direction, labelled currency units and separately calculated duty/tax values; do not claim sample rates are current.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Estimate measurable quantities, choosing a suitable level of precision.
Compare estimated values with measured values to determine absolute differences.
Calculate the percentage error using the actual measurement as the reference value.
Explain how checking measurement error supports sound practical decisions.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can a measured value help us judge the accuracy of an estimate?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Estimate lengths, masses, areas or capacities and measure them with suitable instruments; compare values and calculate percentage errors.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess the actual/estimated values, absolute-error working, reference denominator and percentage representation.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Locate ordered pairs and plot points accurately on Cartesian axes.
Produce the graph of a straight line from a supplied linear equation.
Construct parallel straight lines on a coordinate plane.
Compare gradients to establish when non-vertical lines are parallel.
Construct perpendicular straight lines on the coordinate plane.
Determine how gradients of non-vertical, non-horizontal perpendicular lines are related, including relevant special cases.
Interpret a straight-line graph in a practical setting.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How do positions and gradients on coordinate axes describe lines and their relationships?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Make tables of values, plot line pairs and compare gradients, discussing vertical/horizontal special cases where relevant.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess plotting, graph scales, gradient comparisons and explanation of parallel/perpendicular relationships.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Identify compass directions and distinguish compass from true bearings.
Determine the bearing of one point from another.
Locate a destination using a specified distance and bearing.
Recognise an angle of elevation in a real-world diagram.
Determine an angle of elevation from a measured or drawn situation.
Recognise angles of depression from a horizontal line of sight.
Find angles of depression in diagrams or practical situations.
Use a suitable scale drawing in a simple survey of positions or distances.
Describe applications of scale drawing to real directions or measurements.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can drawings with scale, distance and bearings help locate objects?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Use compass diagrams, map features and three-figure bearings to make a scale plan; sketch sightlines to elevated and depressed objects.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess scale consistency, bearings measured clockwise from north, sightline angles and a correctly labelled survey drawing.
units.core_competency_focus: problem solving, communication and spatial reasoning

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Recognise similar figures and explain their matching-angle and proportional-side properties.
Construct or draw pairs of similar figures accurately.
Describe what remains unchanged and what changes during enlargement.
Enlarge or reduce a plane figure using the properties of enlargement.
Find the linear scale factor between corresponding lengths of similar figures.
Identify practical uses of scale drawings, similarity and enlargement.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can two figures have the same shape but different sizes?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Sort shapes by similarity, measure corresponding sides, draw enlarged images and compare digital or grid-based constructions.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess proportional lengths, scale-factor calculations and accurate enlarged figures.
units.core_competency_focus: problem solving, communication and spatial reasoning

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Identify the angles, hypotenuse and other sides of right-angled triangles.
Express sine, cosine and tangent for an acute angle as appropriate side ratios.
Read trigonometric ratio values for acute angles from mathematical tables.
Find sine, cosine and tangent values using a calculator correctly set to the required angle unit.
Determine unknown sides or angles in a right triangle using trigonometric ratios.
Describe uses of right-triangle trigonometry for measurement problems.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How do changes in a right-triangle angle affect the ratios of its sides?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Label right-angled triangles, compare measured ratios, read tables and use calculators for missing dimensions.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess correct opposite/adjacent/hypotenuse identification, ratio choice and credible side/angle results.

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Choose a sensible class width when organising a numerical data set.
Create a grouped frequency distribution from collected data.
Identify the class interval having the greatest frequency.
Calculate or estimate a mean from grouped data using suitable class values.
Determine the median or median class from a grouped distribution using an appropriate method.
Explain a conclusion drawn from grouped data in an everyday situation.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can grouping observations help reveal the centre and pattern of data?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Collect and tally travel distances or times, arrange frequency classes, identify the modal class and calculate grouped averages.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess class boundaries, totals, modal class and the choice and interpretation of grouped mean/median.
units.core_competency_focus: critical thinking, data literacy and collaboration

manuscript_outcomes.paraphrased_learning_target: Carry out a chance experiment in which basic outcomes are equally likely.
Explain and calculate probability values within the interval from zero to one.
Recognise when two events cannot both occur in a single trial.
Run or model single-trial chance experiments involving mutually exclusive outcomes.
Investigate events in which one trial does not influence the probability of another.
Use a tree diagram to display possible branches of a simple chance process.
Explain how probability reasoning can inform non-gambling everyday decisions.

vibeschool_inquiry_questions: How can experiments and diagrams help us reason about the likelihood of events?
vibeschool_suggested_learning_experience: Use coins, dice and counters to compare equally likely outcomes, independent trials and mutually exclusive events; draw and check branches.
vibeschool_assessment_evidence: Assess probabilities in [0,1], clear event distinctions and correctly labelled probability trees.
